verdict: AMD's revenue jumped 32% to $7.7B on record server and PC chip sales, but an $800M charge on AI chips blocked from China pushed it to an operating loss — an $834M tax benefit still turned the quarter into an $872M net profit.

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: an ~$800M MI308 charge cut it from ~54%

segments.name: Data Center
segments.note: EPYC server processors and Instinct AI accelerators — EPYC demand was strong, but US export controls blocked Instinct MI308 shipments to China.

segments.name: Client
segments.note: Ryzen processors for PCs — a record $2.5B quarter, up 67% on 'Zen 5' desktop chips and a richer product mix.

segments.name: Gaming
segments.note: Graphics cards and console chips — up 73% YoY on Radeon GPU demand and recovering semi-custom console sales.

segments.name: Embedded
segments.note: Chips built into cars, industrial gear and communications equipment (the Xilinx business) — down 4% YoY.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing the next generations of CPUs, GPUs and AI accelerators.

opex.name: Marketing, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling products and running the company.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: Writing down the value of technology bought in acquisitions (Xilinx above all) — a bookkeeping charge, not cash.

otherDetail: Other income of $98M, plus $8M of equity income and $104M from discontinued operations, less $38M of interest expense — a net +$172M.
footerNote: The tax line was a benefit, not a bill: an $834M income-tax benefit (largely non-cash) is drawn as a green source into net profit. Continuing-operations profit was $768M; $104M came from discontinued operations.

takeaways.title: China controls bit hard
takeaways.text: US export controls on the Instinct MI308 AI chip led to roughly $800M of inventory and related charges inside cost of sales — GAAP gross margin was 40%, versus about 54% without the charges.

takeaways.title: PC chips had a record quarter
takeaways.text: Client revenue hit a record $2.5B, up 67% YoY on 'Zen 5' Ryzen desktop processors, and Gaming rose 73% — together they carried the quarter while Data Center absorbed the China hit.

takeaways.title: A tax benefit flipped the bottom line
takeaways.text: AMD booked an $834M income-tax benefit, so despite a $134M operating loss the quarter ended with $872M of net income — $768M from continuing operations plus $104M from the business being sold.

oneTimers: Export-control charges: ~$800M — inventory and related charges on Instinct MI308 AI chips blocked from sale to China, booked inside cost of sales. Excluding them, gross margin would have been about 54% instead of 40%.

Discontinued operations added $104M below the line — profit from the server-rack manufacturing business (acquired with ZT Systems) that AMD agreed to sell; profit from continuing operations was $768M.
An $834M income-tax benefit — largely non-cash — turned an operating loss into a net profit; it is drawn as a green 'Tax benefit' source in the chart.
